tips.title: Airbrushing Vallejo Model Air — Optimal Thinning
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is designed for airbrushing straight from the bottle, but adding a few drops of Vallejo Airbrush Thinner improves atomization. For a 20% thinning, mix 4 parts Model Air with 1 part thinner. Add 2-3 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint for finer nozzle setups. Spray at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure.

tips.title: Base Coat Technique with Tamiya Acrylics
tips.text: Before painting, lightly sand and clean your model. Apply a primer coat with Tamiya Fine Surface Primer (TS-29) using an Iwata Eclipse HP-CS airbrush and 0.3mm needle at 15-20 psi. Let it dry for 24 hours. Apply two thin coats of Tamiya Acrylic paint (e.g., X-16 Sky Grey), thinning with Tamiya Acrylic Thinner (74150) at a 1:1 ratio. Airbrush at 18-25 psi.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Mr. Hobby Tapes
tips.text: Use Mr. Hobby Masking Tapes (99991) for precise camouflage patterns. Measure and mark your pattern on the model, then apply tape along the lines. Burnish edges with a bone folder or skewer to prevent paint bleeding. Airbrush upper colors, let dry, then carefully remove tape before lower colors to avoid paint removal.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes — The Wet Method
tips.text: AK Interactive Washes (AK011 to AK016) can be applied using the wet method for a more controlled effect. Shake the bottle well, then place a few drops on a palette. Dilute with AK Interactive Thinner (AK301) at a 1:1 ratio. Using a soft brush (e.g., Winsor & Newton Series 7), gently stroke the wash onto the model, working it into panel lines and details. Let dry naturally.

tips.title: Chipping Technique with AMMO by Mig Jimenez Chipping Colors
tips.text: AMMO by Mig Jimenez Chipping Colors (AC7001 to AC7006) allow you to replicate chipped paint effectively. Apply the desired color as a base coat. Once dry, lightly dab the sponge (e.g., makeup sponge) in the chipping color, then gently pat the model's edges and areas prone to wear. Let dry, then carefully remove excess using a damp cloth or cotton swab.
